title: Homogeneous residual from normalized finite-coset averaging
statement:
Let $G$ be a topological group, $H\subseteq G$ a subgroup of finite index $m$, and $D$ a transversal for the right cosets $H\backslash G$. Let $n\geq1$, and let $E\subseteq G^{n+1}$ be a subset. Write $B_q(G)=\mathbf Z[G^{q+1}]$ and $B_{-1}(G)=\mathbf Z[\{()\}]$ where $()$ denotes the unique empty tuple, for the free abelian tuple groups with alternating-deletion boundary $\partial$ and the augmentation $\partial[x]=[()]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Suppose $H$-equivariant homomorphisms $A_q:B_q(G)\to B_q(G)$ for $-1\leq q\leq n$ and $Q_q:B_q(G)\to B_{q+1}(G)$ for $-1\leq q\leq n$ satisfy $A_{-1}=1$, $Q_{-1}=0$, $\partial A_q=A_{q-1}\partial$ and
$$1-A_q=\partial Q_q+Q_{q-1}\partial\quad(0\leq q\leq n).$$
Assume each nonnegative-degree $A_q$ and $Q_q$ is a fixed finite integer sum of basis tuples specified by continuous tuple maps, with coefficients independent of the input; assume $A_n[x]$ is an integer sum of tuples in $E$ for every $x$.
Fix a prime $\ell$ and use $\mathbf Q_\ell$ of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. For any topological $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space $V$ with continuous addition and scalar multiplication and trivial group action, a continuous homogeneous cochain of degree $q$ is a continuous function $L:G^{q+1}\to V$; its differential is $\delta L(x)=\sum_i(-1)^iL(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{q+1})$. Write $\widehat F$ for the additive extension of a degree-$n$ function $F$ to $B_n(G)$. Define
$$UF(x)=\widehat F(Q_{n-1}[x]),\quad WF(y)=\widehat F(A_n[y]),\quad (\mathcal M_qL)(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{s\in D}L(sx_0,\ldots,sx_q).$$
Then $\delta^2=0$. Averaging maps continuous diagonally $H$-invariant functions to continuous diagonally $G$-invariant functions, commutes with $\delta$, and fixes $G$-invariant functions. For every continuous diagonally $G$-invariant $F$, both $UF$ and $WF$ are continuous and $H$-invariant. If $\delta F=0$, then
$$F=\delta(UF)+WF,\quad\delta(WF)=0,\quad F=\delta(\mathcal M_{n-1}UF)+\mathcal M_nWF,\quad\delta(\mathcal M_nWF)=0.$$
If $F|_E=0$, then $WF=0$ and $\mathcal M_nWF=0$. The operators $\mathcal M_{n-1}U$ and $\mathcal M_nW$ are linear and are fixed finite sums of evaluations at continuous tuple maps with coefficients $k/m$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, determined solely by $A,Q,D$. No normality of $H$, prime-to-$\ell$ condition on $m$, completeness of $V$, or cohomology quotient is required.

proof.text: For a function $L:G^{q+1}\to V$ define $\widehat L(\sum_j k_j[z_j])=\sum_j k_jL(z_j)$. The unique finite basis expansion in [def-weil-pbc-free-module] makes this a well-defined additive homomorphism. By the displayed deletion formula, $\widehat{\delta L}=\widehat L\partial$ on every basis tuple, hence on every finite chain. Evaluation is linear in $L$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel auxiliary expansion: evaluation of a truncated chain homotopy and normalized right-coset averaging; retained item proof steps 10–11 and coefficient denominator in step 12. Agent-formulated, not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: In $\delta^2L(x_0,\ldots,x_{q+2})$, the tuple omitting original positions $i<j$ occurs twice: deleting $i$ first contributes $(-1)^i(-1)^{j-1}$, and deleting $j$ first contributes $(-1)^j(-1)^i$. These coefficients add to zero, and these pairs exhaust the double sum. Thus $\delta^2=0$, without an invariance assumption. Each deletion is a continuous coordinate projection, so $\delta$ preserves continuity; it also preserves diagonal invariance because deleting coordinates commutes with diagonal translation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel auxiliary expansion: evaluation of a truncated chain homotopy and normalized right-coset averaging; retained item proof steps 10–11 and coefficient denominator in step 12. Agent-formulated, not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: The right coset set is nonempty (it contains $H$), so its finite cardinal $m$ is a positive integer. Since $\mathbf Q_\ell$ has characteristic zero by [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $m$ is nonzero in this field and $m^{-1}$ exists, even when $\ell\mid m$. For each $s\in D$, the tuple translation $\lambda_s(x)=(sx_0,\ldots,sx_q)$ is continuous. Thus $m^{-1}\sum_{s\in D}L\circ\lambda_s$ is continuous whenever $L$ is: each summand is continuous and the sum is finite, using the assumed continuous addition and scalar multiplication.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel auxiliary expansion: evaluation of a truncated chain homotopy and normalized right-coset averaging; retained item proof steps 10–11 and coefficient denominator in step 12. Agent-formulated, not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Fix $a\in G$. Right multiplication $Hs\mapsto Hsa$ permutes $H\backslash G$, with inverse right multiplication by $a^{-1}$. Accordingly there is a permutation $\pi_a$ of $D$ and elements $h_s\in H$ such that $sa=h_s\pi_a(s)$. If $L$ is diagonally $H$-invariant, then $L(sax_0,\ldots,sax_q)=L(\pi_a(s)x_0,\ldots,\pi_a(s)x_q)$. Reindexing the finite sum by $\pi_a$ proves $(\mathcal M_qL)(ax)=\mathcal M_qL(x)$. This uses right cosets and does not require normality.

proof.text: Expanding both sides gives $\delta\mathcal M_qL= m^{-1}\sum_{s\in D}\sum_{i=0}^{q+1}(-1)^iL(sx_0,\ldots,\widehat{sx_i},\ldots,sx_{q+1})=\mathcal M_{q+1}\delta L$. The middle equality only interchanges two finite sums. If $L$ is $G$-invariant, all $m$ summands defining $\mathcal M_qL$ equal $L$, so $\mathcal M_qL=m^{-1}mL=L$.

proof.text: For $F$ as in the statement, the assumed finite continuous tuple expansions of $Q_{n-1}$ and $A_n$ express $UF$ and $WF$ as finite sums $\sum_j k_jF\circ b_j$. Thus both functions are continuous. On chains, $G$-invariance of $F$ gives $\widehat F(hz)=\widehat F(z)$ for $h\in H$. Equivariance of $Q_{n-1}$ gives $UF(hx)=\widehat F(Q_{n-1}[hx])=\widehat F(hQ_{n-1}[x])=UF(x)$; the identical substitution with $A_n$ gives $WF(hy)=WF(y)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel auxiliary expansion: evaluation of a truncated chain homotopy and normalized right-coset averaging; retained item proof steps 10–11 and coefficient denominator in step 12. Agent-formulated, not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Now assume $\delta F=0$. Evaluate $1-A_n=\partial Q_n+Q_{n-1}\partial$ on $[y]$ and apply $\widehat F$. By step 1, $\widehat F(\partial Q_n[y])=\widehat{\delta F}(Q_n[y])=0$, and $\widehat F(Q_{n-1}\partial[y])=\delta(UF)(y)$. Consequently $F-WF=\delta(UF)$. Applying $\delta$ and step 2 gives $\delta(WF)=\delta F-\delta^2(UF)=0$. Only $Q_n$, already among the hypotheses, is used; no endomorphism $A_{n+1}$ is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel auxiliary expansion: evaluation of a truncated chain homotopy and normalized right-coset averaging; retained item proof steps 10–11 and coefficient denominator in step 12. Agent-formulated, not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: Apply $\mathcal M_n$ to the equality in step 7. Steps 4–6 ensure the averaged functions are continuous and $G$-invariant, and step 5 gives $F=\mathcal M_nF=\delta(\mathcal M_{n-1}UF)+\mathcal M_nWF$. Also $\delta(\mathcal M_nWF)=\mathcal M_{n+1}\delta(WF)=0$. The definition of averaging applies in degree $n+1$ independently of the truncated chain maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel auxiliary expansion: evaluation of a truncated chain homotopy and normalized right-coset averaging; retained item proof steps 10–11 and coefficient denominator in step 12. Agent-formulated, not asserted in the blueprint.

proof.text: If $F|_E=0$, evaluate $\widehat F$ on the assumed expansion of $A_n[y]$ into tuples in $E$: every summand is zero. Hence $WF=0$ and its average is zero, whether or not $F$ is a cocycle. Finally write $Q_{n-1}[x]=\sum_jk_j[b_j(x)]$ and $A_n[y]=\sum_jt_j[c_j(y)]$ using the fixed expansions. Then $(\mathcal M_{n-1}UF)(x)=\sum_{s,j}(k_j/m)F(b_j(\lambda_sx))$ and $(\mathcal M_nWF)(y)=\sum_{s,j}(t_j/m)F(c_j(\lambda_sy))$. These are fixed finite lists of continuous tuple maps with the asserted coefficients. Distributing evaluation over $aF+bF\prime$ proves linearity. All operations are finite sums, so no completeness or cohomology quotient is used.
